title: Is it I? (Matthew 26:17–35)
hook: one of you shall betray me, and nobody points across the room
tomorrow: why ask friends to stay up with you, then walk away from them?

segments.voice: Perfume poured out, a name lost, a gift still told: wherever this gospel is preached. Two days later, a table.

When something leaks from a group chat, the replies come fast, and almost all of them point somewhere else. Not me. Must be him. It's the Passover meal. Jesus and the twelve are at the table, eating, when he says it: "Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me." Nobody points across the room. Matthew says they were exceeding sorrowful, and every one of them began to ask the same thing. Not who is it. "Lord, is it I?" And then one more voice asks it too, with one word changed.
screen: `NOT ME. MUST BE HIM.` → `ONE OF YOU SHALL BETRAY ME.` → `LORD, IS IT I?`

segments.voice: Each of them knows his own heart a little, and none is sure of it. Jesus answers with a picture, not a name: "He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me." Then Judas asks, and the word changes. The others said Lord. He says, "Master, is it I?" Jesus answers, "Thou hast said." At that same table Jesus takes bread, blesses it and breaks it: "Take, eat; this is my body." Then the cup: "Drink ye all of it." Christians remember this meal in communion and understand it differently. Catholic and Orthodox Christians speak of the bread and wine becoming his body and blood; other churches speak of a memorial, or of his presence in a spiritual way. They sing a hymn and walk out to the Mount of Olives. On the way, Jesus says they will all stumble this night. Peter is fast: "Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended." Jesus tells him, "Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice." Peter says he'd die first. And Matthew adds one quiet line: "Likewise also said all the disciples." At the table, every one of them asked, is it I? On the road, every one of them was sure it wasn't.
screen: `HE THAT DIPPETH WITH ME.` · `MASTER, IS IT I?` · `TAKE, EAT; THIS IS MY BODY.` · `LIKEWISE ALSO SAID ALL.` · then, large: `IS IT I?`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring up one thing that went wrong this week, between you and someone else. Ask the disciples' question about it, slowly: is it I? Don't rush to an answer or a defense. Just let the question sit at the table with you. If an answer comes, let it be honest and small, the size of one true sentence, and let that be enough for now.
Is it I? The question each disciple asked at the table when Jesus said one of them would betray him.
Your line: is it I? In Matthew, the humbler place to stand was the table, not the road. Until tomorrow.

fork.setup: your friend's church says the bread becomes Christ's body. your church calls it a memorial. she asks what Matthew 26 itself says. the honest answer?
